subject: zoology
question_text: What is the percentage of PAR in the incident solar radiation?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.62, VSAQ 169). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK REDUNDANCY: VSAQ 168 ('What is PAR?') and VSAQ 169 ('What is the percentage of PAR...') are printed as two separate questions on book p.62 with nearly the same one-line answer. Both are authored because both are in the asked bank; this card leads with the percentage and 168 leads with the expansion. The book's own printed wording for 169 is 'What is the percentage of PAR, in the incident solar radiation.' — cleaned to a question here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The percentage
lines: PAR is less than 50% of the incident solar
the part of sunlight that plants can use
steps.why: The question asks for one number, so it is written in the first line; the expansion follows because a bare percentage with no named quantity is not a complete answer.
common_mistakes: Answering 2 to 10%. That is the share of PAR that plants capture, not the share of sunlight that is PAR.
Giving the number without expanding PAR.
steps.memory_tip: Less than half of the sunlight arriving is even usable by a plant.
steps.margin_note: The percentage in the first line, then the expansion. Two short sentences.

steps.label: What plants capture
lines: Of this PAR, green plants capture only
This small fraction supports the whole
steps.why: The second number completes the picture and is the one the long answer on energy flow uses, so writing both here keeps the two figures fixed to the right quantities.
common_mistakes: Adding the two percentages together. They are percentages of DIFFERENT quantities.
Leaving the second number out. A two-mark answer needs a second point.
steps.memory_tip: Two steps down: sunlight to PAR, then PAR to what the plant actually keeps.
steps.margin_note: The second percentage and one line on why so little matters.

insider_note: Lead with the percentage. The number is the mark here, not the definition of PAR.
